# Results (generated by src/run_analysis.py)

Sample: 1997-05 to 2026-10 (monthly; last month with both CPI and Bank Rate).

## Headline (baseline: Taylor 1993, headline CPI, r* = 2%, OBR output gap)

* Peak 2022 shortfall month: **October 2022**
* Rule-implied Bank Rate: **18.2%** (CPI 11.1%, OBR gap +1.03%)
* Actual Bank Rate (month-end): **2.25%**
* Gap: **15.9pp**
* First month the baseline shortfall exceeded 5pp: January 2011

* With a one-month CPI publication lag (rule uses the latest print the MPC had): peak 2022 shortfall 15.1pp in November 2022 (rule 18.1% vs actual 3.00%)

## How much does the neutral-rate assumption explain?

* Cutting r* from 2% to +1.5% closes 0.5pp = 3% of the 15.9pp gap
* Cutting r* from 2% to +1.0% closes 1.0pp = 6% of the 15.9pp gap
* Cutting r* from 2% to +0.5% closes 1.5pp = 9% of the 15.9pp gap
* Cutting r* from 2% to +0.0% closes 2.0pp = 13% of the 15.9pp gap
* Cutting r* from 2% to -0.5% closes 2.5pp = 16% of the 15.9pp gap
* Across all r* (−0.5% to 2%) and all five gap measures (Taylor 1993, headline CPI) the shortfall ranges 12.9–16.7pp.
* Using core CPI with r* = 0.5% still leaves a 7.5pp shortfall.
* Smallest shortfall in the whole grid (any rule, inflation measure, gap, r*): 6.0pp.

## Shortfall by output-gap measure (r* = 2%)

* OBR (Oct 2026 EFO): 15.9pp
* HP filter (two-sided): 16.4pp
* HP filter (real-time): 16.7pp
* HP filter (ex-Covid trend): 15.4pp
* Zero gap: 15.4pp

## Behind the curve over the whole sample

* Months with Bank Rate below the Taylor (1993) rule even at r* = -0.5% (headline CPI): 132 of 354; using core CPI: 138.
* Mean shortfall (baseline) 1997-05 to 2007-12: -1.50pp; 2009-03 to 2019-12: 3.27pp; 2021-01 to 2023-12: 8.82pp; 2024-01 to end: 0.75pp.
